blocks.content: Quiz: Why does wrapping onClose() in useCallback() prevent the Drawer's useEffect() from re-running on every render?
Tap an option below to answer:
Because useCallback() returns the same function reference across renders
useEffect() re-runs when a dependency changes. A stable reference means no change, so no re-run.
useEffect() re-runs when a dependency changes. A stable reference means no change, so no re-run.
Because useCallback() prevents the function from ever being called
useCallback() does not block the function. It only controls when a new function identity is created.
useCallback() does not block the function. It only controls when a new function identity is created.
Because useCallback() caches the function's return value, not the function itself
useCallback() stabilizes the function reference. useMemo() is what caches return values.
useCallback() stabilizes the function reference. useMemo() is what caches return values.
Because useCallback() tells React to skip re-renders of the Drawer component
useCallback() does not control rendering. It only stabilizes function references.
useCallback() does not control rendering. It only stabilizes function references.
